title: Implement CLI commands: cron
description:
Implement cron management CLI commands.

## Commands
- krankie cron install [--hour <0-23>]
- krankie cron uninstall
- krankie cron status

## Behavior
- install: Adds crontab entry for daily check at specified hour (default: random 2-6 AM)
- uninstall: Removes krankie entry from crontab
- status: Shows if installed, next run time

## Implementation
- Use crontab -l and crontab - for manipulation
- Log output to ~/.krankie/check.log

## Acceptance Criteria
- cron install adds valid crontab entry
- cron uninstall removes only krankie entry
- cron status accurately reports state

title: Web Interface — krankie web
description:
# Web Interface for Krankie

## Goal
Add a `krankie web` command that starts a local web server (default port 6768) serving a beautiful shadcn-based web UI for managing ASO — an alternative to the existing TUI.

## Scope
- Dashboard overview (stats, movers, trends)

- Rankings view (current, history charts)
- Ratings view (scores, histograms, trends)

- Real-time updates via polling or WebSocket

description:
## Summary
Improve the keyword add workflow — make it easier to add keywords with country (store) selection.

## Current State
`krankie keyword add <app_id> <keyword> --store <stores>` works but:
- Requires knowing the app's internal ID
- Store defaults to 'us' only
- No validation that the keyword returns results
- No interactive mode in TUI

## CLI Improvements

### Better Defaults & Validation
- After adding, immediately do a quick check and show current rank (if any)
- Validate store codes against a known list of App Store country codes
- Warn if keyword is very long (>50 chars) or very short (<2 chars)

### Batch Add
```bash
krankie keyword add <app_id> --batch "keyword1,keyword2,keyword3" --store us,gb
```
Creates all combinations: keyword1/us, keyword1/gb, keyword2/us, keyword2/gb, etc.

### Interactive Add
```bash
krankie keyword add <app_id> --interactive
```
Prompts for keyword and store, shows preview of what will be added, confirms before saving.

## TUI: Add Keyword View
In the Keywords or AppDetail view, add a keyboard shortcut:
- Press `a` to open an 'Add Keyword' input
- Text input for keyword
- Store selector (cycle with Tab or type code)
- Enter to confirm, Esc to cancel
- Show confirmation with quick rank check result

## Implementation Notes
- Store codes: maintain a list of valid App Store country codes in config
- Quick rank check after add: call `checkRanking()` immediately (single API call)
- Batch mode: reuse existing `addKeyword()` in a loop, handle duplicates gracefully

- `src/cli/commands/keyword.ts` — add `--batch`, `--interactive` flags, quick check after add
- `src/config.ts` — add valid store codes list
- `src/tui/views/Keywords.tsx` — add 'a' key handler, inline add form

title: Keyword Finder — Competitor Analysis Tool
description:
## Epic: Keyword Finder

A competitor analysis tool that discovers keyword opportunities by analyzing what top-ranking apps target.

### User Story
As an indie developer, I want to enter a seed keyword and see what other keywords I should target, based on what competitor apps in the top results are optimizing for.

### Core Workflow
```
krankie keyword find "fitness tracker" --store us
```
1. Search iTunes for seed keyword → get top 10-20 ranked apps
2. Fetch metadata for each competitor app (title, description, genre)
3. Extract keyword candidates from competitor metadata
4. Score candidates by frequency, position weight, and competition
5. Present ranked list of keyword opportunities

### Design Decisions
- **CLI-first** — JSON output for agents, table for humans
- **Shallow by default** — metadata extraction only, no ranking verification (fast, <20 API calls)
- **Deep mode opt-in** — `--depth deep` verifies actual rankings for top candidates (slower, more API calls)
- **No persistent storage** — results are ephemeral analysis; market data changes too fast to cache
- **Compare mode** — `--compare <app_id>` shows keyword gaps (competitors rank, you don't)

### Child Issues
This epic breaks down into:
1. Core keyword extraction engine (scraper/finder)
2. CLI command (`krankie keyword find`)
3. Compare/gap analysis mode
4. TUI integration (optional, later)
close_reason: All child issues implemented: keyword extraction engine and CLI command

title: Keyword extraction engine
description:
## Summary
Build the core engine that extracts keyword candidates from competitor app metadata.

## New File: `src/scraper/finder.ts`

### Types
```typescript
interface KeywordFinderOptions {
  seed: string
  store: string
  platform: Platform
  limit?: number           // max keywords to return (default: 20)
  depth?: 'shallow' | 'deep'  // shallow = metadata only, deep = verify rankings
  minApps?: number         // min competitor apps that use keyword (default: 2)
  topApps?: number         // how many top apps to analyze (default: 10)
}

interface KeywordCandidate {
  keyword: string
  frequency: number        // how many competitor apps use this keyword
  frequencyPct: number     // frequency / total apps analyzed
  foundIn: ('title' | 'description' | 'genre')[]
  wordCount: number
  longTail: boolean        // 3+ words
  sources: { appId: string; appName: string; rank: number }[]
}

interface KeywordFinderResult {
  seed: string
  store: string
  platform: string
  analyzedApps: number
  apiCalls: number
  elapsed: string
  keywords: KeywordCandidate[]
  competitors: { appId: string; name: string; rank: number }[]
}
```

### Core Algorithm
1. `searchKeyword(seed, store, platform)` — get top 200 results
2. Take top N apps (default 10)
3. `lookupAppDetails(appId, store)` for each — get full metadata
4. Extract keywords from each app:
   - **Title**: split on spaces/punctuation, extract 1-4 word n-grams (weight: 3.0)
   - **Description**: first 500 chars, extract 1-3 word n-grams (weight: 1.0)
   - **Genre**: use as-is (weight: 0.5)
5. Normalize: lowercase, trim, remove stop words (the, a, an, and, or, for, with, etc.)
6. Deduplicate and count frequency across apps
7. Filter: remove seed keyword itself, keywords <2 or >50 chars, keywords appearing in <minApps apps
8. Score and rank by: frequency * position_weight
9. Return top N results

### Keyword Extraction Details
- Use n-gram approach: for "Best Fitness Tracker Free" extract:
  - 1-grams: best, fitness, tracker, free
  - 2-grams: best fitness, fitness tracker, tracker free
  - 3-grams: best fitness tracker, fitness tracker free
  - 4-grams: best fitness tracker free
- Weight n-grams by source (title > description > genre)
- Deduplicate: if "fitness tracker" appears in 8/10 apps, that's high signal

### Deep Mode (Optional)
When `depth === 'deep'`:
- After scoring, take top 10 keyword candidates
- For each, call `searchKeyword(candidate, store, platform)` to verify real rankings
- Add `avgRank` and `competition` fields based on actual search results
- This adds ~10 more API calls but gives much more accurate data

### Rate Limiting
- Use existing `ratelimit.ts` delay between requests
- Report progress via callback: `onProgress?: (msg: string) => void`

- `src/scraper/finder.ts` — the extraction engine

## Files to Modify

Implement ranking query CLI commands.

## Commands
- krankie rankings [--app <app_id>] [--keyword <keyword>] [--store <store>] [--days <n>] [--json]
- krankie rankings movers [--days <n>] [--min-change <n>] [--json]
- krankie rankings history <keyword_id> [--days <n>] [--json]

## Acceptance Criteria
- All commands support --json
- movers shows biggest rank changes (up or down)
- history shows full time-series for a keyword
- Default --days is 7
